source_title: Flashing red Mid-, small-caps under pressure; Suzlon, Swiggy, STL, HFCL plunge up to 10%
source_excerpt: Shares of midcap and smallcap companies were under pressure with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices falling by up to 2 per cent each in intraday trade after a sharp decline in the stock prices of Suzlon Energy, Swiggy, Sterlite Technologies (STL) and HFCL. At 12:31 PM, the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 index were down 0.60 per cent and 1.24 per cent, respectively. In comparison, the Nifty 50 was up 0.62 per cent. However, in the past four trading days, the Nifty Midcap 100 index rallied 4 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index surged 6 per cent, against a 1.5 per cent gain in the Nifty 50 till Thursday. Suzlon Energy, Blue Star Company, Swiggy, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, Dixon Technologies, Tube Investments of India, UPL and Voltas from the Nifty Midcap 100 index declined between 4-10 per cent Sigility, Cohance Lifesciences, Redington, Emmvee Photovoltaic Power, Welspun Corp, Kirloskar Oil Engines, R R Kabel, Pine Labs, Computer Age Management Services, STL, HFCL, IFCI, MTAR Technologies, Inox Wind and Amber Enterprises from the Nifty Smallcap 100 index were down in the range of 5-7 per cent in intraday trade. Among individual stocks, Suzlon Energy tanked 10 per cent to ₹33.23, hitting a multiyear low on the NSE in intraday trade. The stock quoted at its lowest level since November 2023, as analysts believe margins and growth prospects for Suzlon would be under pressure FY28 onwards due to limited India market (7–8GW pa) and increasing competition (15–20GW industry capacity), not to mention growing pains of a single-product company. All in all, analysts at JM Financial Institutional Equities said they are downgrading Suzlon to ADD (from BUY) with a revised target price of ₹40 (earlier ₹46) based on 12x Sep’28E earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) (implied 20x Sep’28 EPS). The stock hit a record low of ₹174.20 on October 26, 2026. A combined 22.6 million shares changed hands on the NSE and BSE. ICICI Securities in a note said that volatility is expected to remain elevated, supported by heightened Middle East geopolitical tensions, rising Brent crude oil prices, and cautious positioning ahead of the US midterm elections. "The crude oil headwind is getting stronger with Brent rising above $117. There are reports of the US likely resuming strikes against Iran after the mid-term elections which are due on November 3rd. Even though FII selling has turned weak with occasional buys in recent days, the market construct appears unfavourable for a rally,” said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. An interesting trend is the rally in the small-cap segment after the brutal selloff during last week. Since the selloff was triggered by forced liquidation of margin-funded long positions, DIIs and investors are using the opportunity to buy growth stocks in this segment despite their high valuations. Sustained capital flows into mid-and small-cap funds facilitate accumulation of these stocks. However, investors should keep in mind the fact that value buying opportunities are in large-caps which are temporarily out of favour due to FII selling, said V K Vijayakumar. Meanwhile, the market outlook for the week ahead points to cautious consolidation as domestic equities balance corporate earnings against global macroeconomic headwinds. Investors will monitor foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows, global rate trajectories, energy prices, and bond yields for market direction. Domestically, ongoing quarterly earnings, economic data releases, and underlying liquidity will drive stock-specific momentum, said Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura.
